items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 14 at 10:02AM AKDT until September 16 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 2 to 4 feet above the mean high tide line.

* WHERE...Hooper Bay and Scammon Bay.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Tuesday to 1 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur. In Scammon Bay,
water may reach up to the boat launch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water may rise along the Kun River and
typical low lying areas may see minor inundation.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued September 14 at 9:47AM AKDT until September 14 at 11:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Visibility as low as one quarter mile in dense fog.

* WHERE...Fairbanks Metro Area.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.
items.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 14 at 9:47AM AKDT until September 15 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Windy Pass.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 10 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Wind gusts up to 40 mph possible along the
Parks Hwy towards Anderson. There is a chance wind gusts could be
stronger depending on the track and strength of the low moving
across the YK Delta.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 14 at 6:08AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* Monday evening through Wednesday afternoon. Heaviest rainfall
expected through Tuesday evening.

Rainfall:

* Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches Monday through Wednesday likely
won't be high enough for widespread flooding, but smaller
tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including Willow Creek and the
Little Susitna will likely reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concer

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 14 at 6:02AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
